slideDifferences.nativeText:
When we talk plans, we normally work in English using the “going to” structure. Check the following examples.
TO CONSIDER

Going to is a fixed structure that denotes future. 
The verbs after this grammatical structure go in simple form. 
 The future phrases at the end can be specific or general.
Going to
She is going to work as a community manager in the future.
Is she going to work as a community manager in the future?
They are going to become good traders at this rate.
Are they going to become good traders at this rate?
I am going to hitchhike so I can become a trip blogger.
Are you going to hitchhike so you can become a trip blogger?

texts: Functional English
Language Targets
Aspects
Examples

Talk about plans or actions in the future that may happen or not. 
 -They can change-

She is going to start uploading videos as an influencer on Instagram. 

I am going to travel so I can become a blogger. 

They are going to spend the weekend at home.
When using “going to” we can consider the following function in the future.
TO CONSIDER
Any action can be inserted here, not only talking about occupations.

texts: Children Chit chat!
You know what? I am going to become a YouTuber
when I get older.
No way! It is better to work as a trader.
I am going to be one of the best traders ever.
Well, that too. Hey, how about VR developer? Joe’s brother is
going to start working at a VR company as a developer.
Amazing! When is he going to start working there?
I guess on July, but I am going to ask Joe to confirm.
Do you think he is going to get free demos to try?
I hope he does! So maybe, we are going to be able to play with Joe.
OMG! If that is true, we are going to be the luckiest kids on the block.
Totally! I am going to ask Joe now. Let’s go!
C. Read the following dialogue and state if the sentences are true (T) or false (F). After that, read the dialogue aloud with your teacher.
1.  Kid number 1 wants to be a YouTuber.	 (T) (F)
2. The other kid is going to become a
YouTuber too.	  				 (T) (F)
3. Joe is going to work as a VR developer.	 (T) (F)
4. Joe’s brother is going to start in February.	 (T) (F)
5.  Joe’s brother is going to get free demos.	     (T) (F)
6.  They are going to play with Joe
if his brother gets demos.			     (T) (F)
7.  They are not going to be the luckiest kids
from the block.					     (T) (F)
8.  They are going to ask Joe about it now.	     (T) (F)
